Choose Koh Samui for easy flights, the widest choice of hotels, private hospitals and family comfort. Choose Koh Phangan for the Full Moon Party, yoga and wilder beaches, and Koh Tao for diving and snorkelling. Many people base themselves on Samui and visit the others: Phangan is 20–50 minutes away by boat and Koh Tao 1 h 30–2 h by fast boat.

The verdict in one box

IslandBest forSkip it if
Koh SamuiFirst visits, short trips, families, honeymoons, comfort, a mix of beach days and boat tripsYou want backpacker prices or a remote, undeveloped island
Koh PhanganThe Full Moon and Half Moon parties, yoga and wellness, quiet northern beaches, longer staysYou need an airport on the island or private-hospital care close by
Koh TaoLearning to dive, snorkelling, viewpoints, a small-island feelYou don't dive or snorkel, travel with toddlers, or dislike steep roads

Can't decide? Stay on Samui and see the other two on day trips: our Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat trip (2,200 THB) covers Tao, and a private speedboat to Koh Phangan or the Full Moon Party speedboat (1,400 THB return) covers Phangan.

Koh Samui is best for…

Ease and comfort. Samui is the only one of the three with an airport, with about 20–25 flights a day from Bangkok Suvarnabhumi, so a long weekend or a one-week holiday loses no time in transit. It has the widest range of hotels, from 500 THB guesthouses to some of Thailand's most expensive resorts, a 51 km ring road, Grab, car hire, Central Samui mall and several private hospitals.

Families and couples. Choeng Mon is one of the calmest bays in the Gulf, Lipa Noi is shallow enough for toddlers at high tide, and the north-east resorts are 5–15 minutes from the airport. Honeymooners have the pick of pool villas on the west coast and around Choeng Mon.

Boat days. Samui is the launch point for Ang Thong Marine Park (42 islands about 30 km west, open 16 December to 31 October), Pig Island and Koh Tan (all year from Thong Krut), and day trips to Koh Tao and Koh Phangan. See Koh Samui tours.

The trade-offs: Samui is the most developed and the dearest of the three, Chaweng is busy and has traffic, and the big east-coast beaches get surf and red flags from October to December. Read the Koh Samui travel guide.

Koh Phangan is best for…

Parties. The Full Moon Party at Haad Rin is one of the best-known beach parties in the world. The next dates are 24 November 2026 (also Loy Krathong night), 24 December and 31 December 2026, then 22 January and 22 February 2027. The Half Moon Festival in Ban Tai, the Jungle Experience and the Waterfall Party fill other nights of the month.

Yoga and wellness. Phangan is the Gulf's yoga and retreat hub, with dozens of studios and long-stay communities, particularly on the west coast.

Quieter, wilder beaches. Away from Haad Rin, the north and east coasts have bays such as Thong Nai Pan and Bottle Beach, plus jungle waterfalls and a national park.

The trade-offs: no airport, rougher roads, fewer upmarket hotels, and Haad Rin is crowded and loud around the full moon. Everything about the island, including its own tours and villas, is on our sister site kohphangan.com. See also Koh Phangan from Samui.

Koh Tao is best for…

Diving. Koh Tao is one of the world's busiest places to learn to dive, and dive courses cost less there than on Samui: an Open Water course is about 14,000 THB if you start on Koh Tao, against about 18,000 THB as a package from Samui including ferries and accommodation. Sail Rock, the best dive site in the area, lies between Tao and Phangan.

Snorkelling. Shallow reefs sit off many of Koh Tao's bays, and Koh Nang Yuan, three islets joined by a sandbar just off the north-west coast, is one of the most photographed spots in Thailand. Its landing fee is 250 THB in cash, and plastic bottles, fins and drones are not allowed.

Small-island atmosphere. Tao is about 21 km², with steep hills, viewpoints and short distances. Sairee is the main beach and village.

The trade-offs: steep, rough roads that are dangerous on a scooter, limited medical facilities, little to do if you don't go in the water, and the longest crossing from Samui (1 h 30–2 h). See Koh Tao and diving from Koh Samui.

Beaches compared

Samui has the long, classic beaches: about 7 km of fine white sand at Chaweng, 4 km at Lamai, and sheltered Choeng Mon. The north and west coasts are tidal, with shallow flats at low tide. Bophut and Bang Rak are not swimming beaches.

Phangan has more variety and more empty coves. Haad Rin Sunrise is the party beach; the north (Thong Nai Pan, Bottle Beach) is quieter and greener; the west coast has sunset beaches with shallow water at low tide.

Tao has small bays rather than long beaches. Sairee is the longest; the rest are coves, many reached by steep tracks, that are best for snorkelling.

All three get surf on east-facing beaches in the north-east monsoon. See Koh Samui beaches.

Nightlife and parties compared

Phangan is the party island, built around the moon: the Full Moon Party at Haad Rin (entry about 200 THB at the gate), the Half Moon Festival in Ban Tai and several jungle parties each month. Samui has the most variety on any night of the week: beach clubs and fire shows in Chaweng, cover bands, cabaret, Muay Thai at two stadiums (no fights on Thursdays) and the Friday walking street at Fisherman's Village. Tao has a lively but small bar scene in Sairee that winds down early compared with Chaweng.

A popular combination is to stay on Samui and cross for the party: our shared Full Moon Party speedboat costs 1,400 THB per person return with hotel pickup and drop-off on Samui. See Full Moon Party from Koh Samui and Koh Samui nightlife.

Diving and snorkelling compared

For diving, Koh Tao wins: it has the most dive schools, the cheapest courses and the shortest boat rides to most sites. Phangan is closest to Sail Rock. From Samui, dive centres run day trips to Sail Rock and Koh Tao (a two-dive Sail Rock day costs from about 4,650 THB), which works well if you want to dive once or twice during a Samui holiday.

For snorkelling, all three work. From Samui, the best days out are Ang Thong (from 16 December to 31 October), Koh Tan on the Pig Island tour, and Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan. The Gulf diving season runs from February to October, with the clearest water in March and April. See snorkelling.

Families

Samui is the easiest island with children: a direct flight, short transfers to Choeng Mon or Chaweng, calm bays, supermarkets, international hospitals and a wide choice of family resorts and pool villas. Our boat trips provide children's life jackets, which must be worn, and infants aged 0–2 travel free.

Phangan suits families who want quiet beaches and a slower pace, especially in the north, but transfers are longer and the roads rougher. Tao is best for families with older children who swim and snorkel confidently; steep roads and limited healthcare make it harder with toddlers. See Koh Samui with kids.

Wellness and yoga

Phangan is the yoga island, with the largest concentration of yoga schools, teacher trainings and long-stay retreats in the Gulf. Samui is the luxury wellness island: destination spas and detox resorts such as Kamalaya near Laem Set, resort spas, Muay Thai camps and golf at Santiburi. Tao is about the water, with little organised wellness. See Koh Samui retreats and spas.

Healthcare and safety

Samui has the best medical care of the three: Bangkok Hospital Samui, Samui International Hospital, Thai International Hospital and Bandon International Hospital are private, and Koh Samui Hospital near Nathon is the government hospital. Phangan has a government hospital and private clinics, including a branch of Bandon International. On Tao, clinics handle minor injuries and serious cases are transferred off the island.

The main risks are the same on all three islands: scooter crashes (ride with a helmet and an International Driving Permit), rip currents on east-facing beaches in the monsoon, and box jellyfish (9 of Thailand's 10 recorded deaths since 2002 were off Samui and Phangan; treat stings with vinegar for 30 seconds or more). Phangan adds party-night risks such as drink spiking. Emergency numbers are the same everywhere: ambulance 1669, Tourist Police 1155. See Koh Samui hospitals.

Costs compared

Samui is the dearest of the three, mainly because of flight prices and its resort market. Mid-range rooms on Samui cost about 1,000–7,000 THB a night depending on the area. Phangan and Tao have more budget bungalows and hostels and generally lower room prices, though top resorts on all three islands are expensive. Day-to-day costs (street food, massages, scooters) are in a similar range on all three. The cheapest place to learn to dive is Koh Tao. See is Koh Samui expensive?

Where to stay on each island

  • Koh Samui: Chaweng for a first visit and nightlife, Choeng Mon for families, Bophut for food, Lamai for value, Maenam for budget and long stays, the west coast for sunsets and villas. See where to stay on Koh Samui.
  • Koh Phangan: Haad Rin only if you are there for the party; Thong Sala and the west coast for convenience and sunsets; the north for quiet beaches.
  • Koh Tao: Sairee for restaurants and dive schools; Mae Haad near the pier; the quieter south and east bays for snorkelling and calm.

Day trips from Samui or a stay on each island?

Day trips from a Samui base make sense if you have a week or less, travel with children, or want one hotel. Koh Phangan is close enough for an easy day by scheduled boat or private speedboat, and our Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat trip covers Tao in 8–9 hours with snorkelling, lunch and the Nang Yuan viewpoint.

Staying on each island makes sense if you have 10 days or more, want to dive properly on Tao, or want several nights on Phangan's beaches. Note that our tour boats return to the island they left from; there is no one-way island hopping on tour boats, so use the scheduled ferries to move between islands. Our Ang Thong tours (1,800 THB by speedboat; closed 1 November–15 December) start and end on Samui. See Ang Thong speedboat tour and islands near Koh Samui.

Same weather on all three?

Yes. Samui, Phangan and Tao all sit in the Gulf of Thailand and share one climate: the calmest, driest months are February to April, May to September is warm with short showers and mostly calm sea, and the north-east monsoon brings the rain and rough sea from October to December, peaking in November (about 445 mm on Samui). That is the opposite pattern to Phuket and Krabi, which are wettest from May to October. In the monsoon, crossings between the islands are choppier and some sailings are cancelled in strong wind, so leave a buffer day before an international flight. See Koh Samui weather.
